hypothesis.text: Make the three customer-level destroy operators use a destruction-local customer-to-route mapping and defer global solution normalization until their full removal batch is complete. Initialize the mapping from the incumbent routes, remove each selected customer directly from its mapped `_Route` while maintaining that route’s load and cost, update only the local mapping/list of live customers needed by worst and Shaw selection, then call `remove_empty_routes()` exactly once before returning the removed list. Preserve each operator’s RNG draws, candidate ordering, removal scoring, q bound, and route-removal implementation; the changed mechanism is solely elimination of repeated whole-solution index rebuilds during a single destroy phase. This leaves the repaired candidate’s implicit-depot sequences, exact coverage, capacity checks, scheduler feasibility validation, and route-limit-first rejection unchanged, but reduces ALNS-core overhead so more destroy/repair/VNS trajectories can execute within the fixed deadline. Measure identical structural/fleet behavior first, then reduced destruction time/increased ALNS iterations and paired final total_distance among equal-fleet feasible results.
hypothesis.target_weakness: Random, worst, and Shaw destruction repeatedly call `_remove_customer`, and each removal invokes `solution.remove_empty_routes()`/`rebuild_index()`, recalculating every route and rebuilding global customer maps up to q times before repair begins. With q sampled at 10–40% of customers, this is avoidable ALNS-core work; unlike the previously unsuccessful repair-batching attempt, destruction only needs route membership during the removal batch and can preserve the exact selected removal sequence.
hypothesis.expected_effect: Lower per-iteration ALNS-core time for q-customer destroy phases and increased fixed-budget search throughput, with no semantic relaxation; seek lower final total_distance only after unchanged fleet_violation and feasibility are confirmed.

hypothesis.text: Remove the redundant `_relocate` entry from `_default_vns_operators`, retaining `_or_opt_1` as the sole single-customer inter-route relocation neighborhood. `_or_opt_1` already tests length-one segments, whose sole orientation is unchanged, applies the same capacity condition, scans the same destination positions, and commits a strictly improving relocation with the existing route recalculation, empty-route cleanup, index rebuild, and deadline polling. This eliminates the duplicate no-improvement scan after every VNS restart without weakening the set of feasible one-customer relocation transitions; it also preserves implicit-depot route representation, customer coverage, hard capacity feasibility, route-count semantics, scheduler route-limit rejection, and the external solve interface. The expected effect is lower embedded-VNS time and more ALNS iterations within the fixed budget, with fleet_violation unchanged and lower final total_distance among equal-fleet feasible runs.
hypothesis.target_weakness: The default VNS runs `_relocate` immediately before `_or_opt_1`, although both enumerate the same inter-route single-customer relocation states with the same source-route/customer/destination/insertion ordering and select the best destination for the first source customer having an improving move. Thus, whenever no relocate exists, VNS pays for two equivalent full neighborhood scans; under the budget-exhausting champion, embedded VNS is the dominant runtime phase. The successful prior exact Or-opt scoring studies further indicate that making this relocation path cheaper increases completed ALNS work and can improve distance without fleet regression.

hypothesis.text: Replace iteration-count cooling with deadline-fraction cooling in `_SimulatedAnnealing`. Add a method that derives temperature directly as the existing geometric interpolation from `start_temp` to `end_temp` at a clamped elapsed fraction, and have the scheduler set that fraction immediately before each acceptance decision from its existing ALNS start time, local time limit, and exit reserve; invoke the same update on early rejected/error iterations so the next decision is also synchronized to consumed budget. Keep the current cost-relative endpoint temperatures, Metropolis acceptance probability, and all destroy/repair, feasibility, capacity, coverage, route-limit rejection, incumbent/best, and external `solve` semantics unchanged. This makes exploration concentrate in the early actual budget and convergence occur near the real deadline despite heterogeneous iteration costs, aiming to reduce late uphill drift or premature trapping and improve final total_distance while preserving fleet_violation.
hypothesis.target_weakness: The simulated-annealing schedule cools once per ALNS iteration using `max(100, time_limit * 50)` as an assumed iteration count, but observed completed ALNS throughput varies substantially with instance and VNS/repair cost (from roughly 4–43 iterations per second in the supplied screening traces). Under the budget-exhausting runtime model, this makes the temperature at a given fraction of the actual deadline depend on incidental neighborhood cost rather than search progress: expensive trajectories can remain too permissive late while cheap trajectories can freeze early.
